title.en: Republic Day and the symbols of India

text.en: It is 26 January. Children gather around the flagpole, the head teacher pulls the rope and the tricolour opens to drums and claps. Everyone sings the National Anthem.

We celebrate 26 January as Republic Day. On this day in 1950 India decided to follow the Constitution, our special book of rules.
India became independent on 15 August 1947. Before that we were not free to take decisions ourselves, and many brave people struggled to make India free.
A country needs rules to run smoothly and keep everyone safe and happy, just as a school does.
In our flag, saffron stands for strength and courage, white for peace and truth, and green for growth and prosperity. The blue Ashoka Chakra at the centre stands for duty, or dharma.
The Republic Day parade in New Delhi has the Defence Forces, state tableaux, fighter jets and cultural programmes.
Look at a currency note. It shows Mahatma Gandhi, a smaller image of him seen when held to light, and a monument. The round spectacles are the symbol of the Swachh Bharat Abhiyan, the Clean India Mission.
Some notes have raised prints to help people with visual impairment, and the MANI app helps them identify notes.
The National Emblem has three lions on a circular platform with the Ashoka Chakra below. It stands for strength, courage and confidence.
Lions once roamed large areas of India. Today they live only in the Gir forests of Gujarat, and efforts to save them have raised their numbers to several hundred.
National symbols remind us who we are. The tiger is our national animal and the peacock our national bird. States have their own animal, bird, tree and flower too.

problem.en: What do the colours of our flag stand for?

text.en: Saffron at the top: strength and courage.
White in the middle: peace and truth, with the Ashoka Chakra for duty.
Green at the bottom: growth and prosperity.

prompt.en: Why do we celebrate Republic Day on 26 January?

requiredIdeas.en: The Constitution was adopted on 26 January 1950
It is different from Independence Day

commonMisconceptions.en: Mixing up Independence Day and Republic Day

points.en: Republic Day marks the Constitution of 1950.
Flag colours: strength, peace, growth, with the Ashoka Chakra for duty.
The emblem, tiger and peacock are national symbols.
